No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.

Reason: To comply with the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems, the National Planning Policy Framework (Paragraph 103), the London Plan (Policies SI 12 and SI 13) along with associated guidance to these policies and Hillingdon Council's Local Plan Policy EM6.

The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan produced by GHA Tree Aboricultural Consultancy reference GHA/DS/160278:26 dated 10th March 2026, including the tree protection measures and methodology for the construction and excavation of the basement. All tree protection measures shall be installed prior to the commencement of the relevant construction works and shall be retained and maintained for the duration of the works in accordance with the approved details.

In particular, the excavation and construction of the basement adjacent to the retained tree shall be undertaken in accordance with the methodology specified within the approved Arboricultural Method Statement, and no excavation, over-dig, storage of materials, plant movement or other construction activity shall take place within the Root Protection Area except where expressly permitted by the approved Arboricultural Method Statement.
All wo

Prior to the commencement of development, including any demolition, excavation or site clearance works, protective fencing for all trees to be retained shall be erected in accordance with the approved Tree Protection Plan within Appendix A of the Arboricultural Method Statement reference GHA/DS/160278:26 dated 10th March 2026, and the recommendations of BS 5837:2012 - Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction.

The protective fencing shall be retained in position for the duration of the construction works and shall not be moved, removed or altered without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority. The protected areas shall be kept clear of all construction activities and shall not be used for the storage of materials, plant or equipment, excavation, changes in ground levels or vehicular access.

In the event that any significant tree roots are encountered during excavation or construction of the basement within or immediately adjacent to the Root Protection Area of any retained tree, works within the affected area shall cease immediately. The roots shall not be cut, severed or otherwise damaged and shall be appropriately protected pending inspection by a suitably qualified arboriculturist.

Details of the roots encountered, together with any necessary amendments to the construction methodology and/or additional tree protection measures, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, following consultation with the Council's Tree Officer. The relevant works shall not recommence until the measures have been approved and shall thereafter be undertaken in accordance with the approved details.

The basement development hereby approved shall be carried out in full accordance with the Basement Impact Assessment & SUDS Report produced by Nimbus Engineer Consultants.

The excavation and construction of the basement shall be inspected and monitored throughout the relevant stages of construction by the author(s) of the approved Basement Impact Assessment, or by an alternative suitably qualified Chartered Structural Engineer or Chartered Civil Engineer with appropriate experience in basement construction.

The appointed engineer shall oversee the works to ensure that the basement is implemented in accordance with the methodologies, recommendations and mitigation measures contained within the approved Basement Impact Assessment.

Nuisance from demolition and construction works is subject to control under The Control of Pollution Act 1974, the Clean Air Acts and other related legislation. In particular, you should ensure that the following are complied with:-

A. Demolition and construction works which are audible at the site boundary shall only be carried out between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 hours Monday to Friday and between the hours of 08.00 hours and 13.00 hours on Saturday. No works shall be carried out on Sundays, Bank or Public Holidays.
B. All noise generated during such works shall be controlled in compliance with British Standard Code of Practice BS 5228:2009.
C. Dust emissions shall be controlled in compliance with the Mayor of London's Best Practice Guidance' The Control of dust and emissions from construction and demolition.
D. No bonfires that create dark smoke or nuisance to local residents.
